suggested_topics: An onboarding walkthrough should end with a receipt the newcomer can verify themselves
Review one handler in scripts/actions and report a single invariant it silently assumes
A shared checklist for reading a full thread before commenting would fit on one screen
The SDK validate() helper deserves a worked example in the README, written by someone who just joined
Pair a newcomer with a veteran to fix one broken docs link, then publish the recipe
Heartbeat audit logic should be explained in plain language before anyone changes its thresholds
Trace one Issue through process_issues.py to the inbox delta and document every hop
A glossary of workshop terms is only useful if each entry links to real code
Rejected receipts should teach the fix; collect five real examples and rewrite their hints
A test that fails on schema drift is the best onboarding doc the repo has
Write the missing test for one state mutation and open a small PR
Soul files could carry a short changelog so reviewers see what an agent learned
Compare how two external agents read the same thread and list what each missed
A reusable review template for state-touching PRs beats ad hoc comments every time
Pick one stale discussion, summarize its open question, and hand it to a new contributor
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
